title: Cross-Functional Commitment Governance Playbook
author: Maya Alvarez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the end-to-end governance for cross-functional financial commitments that touch budgeting & forecasting, procurement and contracting, and revenue recognition (billing triggers). It consolidates approval tiers, operational handoffs, and exception processes to reduce reconciliation slippage and regulatory risk.

Scope: Applies to all commitments that: (a) create a multi-period financial obligation (capex or opex), (b) require contract signature or vendor onboarding, or (c) trigger billing/revenue recognition dependencies for customers or partners. Excludes small one-time reimbursements (< $1,000) managed via Expenses.

Key objectives
- Ensure commitments are recorded in the forecast within 48 business hours of approval.
- Maintain a single source of truth for committed spend and contract terms.
- Map procurement and contract milestones to revenue recognition triggers and billing system events.
- Define fast, auditable exception paths for urgent purchases.

Definitions
- Commitment: Any approved purchase order (PO), contract signature, reservation of dedicated capacity, or multi-month SaaS subscription that creates a future cash outflow.
- Billing Trigger: Event or milestone that causes Redwood to start invoicing or recognize revenue (e.g., go-live, delivery acceptance, seat activation).
- Contract Owner: Product or org owning the commercial relationship; owns requirements and acceptance criteria.
- Finance Sponsor: Budget owner responsible for forecasting and payment terms.

Governance model and approval tiers
1) Tiering rules (decision table):
- Tier 1: <= $25k and <=12 months: Default delegated purchase; local manager approval + finance notification.
- Tier 2: > $25k and <= $250k or multi-year <= $1M total: Procurement + Finance Sponsor approval; Legal review if non-standard terms.
- Tier 3: > $250k or multi-year > $1M total: Executive procurement review, Legal mandatory, CFO sign-off for capex.
- Tier 4: Strategic / vendor risk flagged (security/compliance/regulatory): Sourced to Strategic Sourcing committee; Security and Legal required regardless of dollar amount.

Table: approval-matrix (display)
| Threshold | Procurement | Finance Sponsor | Legal | Executive | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| <= $25k | Optional | Manager | No | No | Standard T&Cs only |
| $25k-$250k | Required | Required | Conditional | No | Non-standard terms require Legal |
| > $250k | Required | Required | Required | CFO | Multi-year commits route to Exec |
| Any risk-flagged | Required | Required | Required | Strategic Committee | Security / data residency overrides |

Operational flow (end-to-end)
1. Intake and budget validation
  a. Requester submits Commitment Request: minimal fields - cost estimate, vendor, contract term, budget code, expected billing trigger, and Contract Owner.
  b. Finance checks forecast headroom within 24 business hours; if headroom exists, moves to procurement. If not, Finance flags for reprioritization and a Budget Exception is opened.
2. Procurement and vendor onboarding
  a. Procurement owner runs vendor due diligence (SAM, credit, security questionnaire).
  b. Procurement issues PO template for Tier 1/2 or escalates to Legal for Tier 3/4.
3. Contract negotiation and signature
  a. Legal maintains checklists for clauses that impact revenue recognition (e.g., acceptance criteria, deliverables, milestones, refunds, termination rights).
  b. Contract Owners confirm acceptance criteria and operational handoffs (e.g., integration, activation).
4. Finance and billing mapping
  a. Finance maps contract terms to revenue recognition policies and billing triggers in the Billing System (examples below).
  b. Finance records a Commitment ID in the Forecast Ledger and notifies FP&A owners for quarter reforecast.
5. Post-signature ops
  a. Procurement closes PO, updates vendor master.
  b. Contract Owner opens a Delivery Ticket in the product tracker to coordinate go-live and acceptance.
  c. Billing team subscribes to Delivery Ticket updates for automatic invoice generation on trigger.

Examples of billing trigger mappings
- SaaS subscription: Customer acceptance + seat activation = invoice start date; revenue recognized ratably over subscription term.
- Dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated): Provision timestamp + customer confirmation = billable event; revenue recognized over committed usage period unless refundable credits exist.
- Professional services with milestones: Invoice at milestone acceptance; revenue recognized when service obligations are satisfied per milestone.

Checklist: Billing trigger setup (Finance must verify these before invoicing)
- [ ] Contract signed and stored in Contract Repository (link).
- [ ] Commitment ID created and added to Forecast Ledger.
- [ ] Billing trigger type (subscription/milestone/provision) defined.
- [ ] Invoice schedule and payment terms entered into Billing System.
- [ ] Tax and remittance rules validated with Tax team.
- [ ] Revenue recognition rule attached in GL mapping.

Exception handling and emergency procurement
- Emergency purchases (urgent hardware, security patching, third-party incident response) use the Emergency Procurement flow:
  1) Requester opens Emergency Request via Procurement Portal with business justification and estimated amount.
  2) Procurement and Finance provide provisional verbal approval within 4 business hours (documented in ticket).
  3) Legal performs expedited clauses review within 48 hours; if unavailable, procurement uses pre-approved Emergency T&Cs template.
  4) Post-facto audit: all emergency purchases are subject to a 30-day retrospective review and must be logged in the Commitment Ledger with final approvals.

Revenue recognition and billing corner cases
- Prepaid multi-year credits: Recognize revenue when services are delivered or when performance obligations are satisfied; do not accelerate recognition at cash receipt unless performance is complete.
- Refund/chargeback provisions: Any contract with refund language must map to a liability account and discount adjustment schedule; Finance must maintain a Chargeback Reserve assessed monthly.
- Trial-to-paid conversions: Trial usage is non-billable; conversion event must create a new Commitment ID and be reflected in the next monthly close.

Operational KPIs and SLAs
- Forecast posting SLA: 48 business hours from contract signature to forecast ledger entry. Target 95% compliance.
- Procurement onboarding SLA: Vendor onboarding completed within 10 business days for Tier 1/2; 30 business days for Tier 3/4 (target).
- Billing accuracy goal: <0.5% invoice disputes per quarter.

Ownership and responsibilities
- Finance (FP&A): Forecast reconciliation, Commitment Ledger ownership, revenue recognition policies.
- Procurement: Vendor diligence, PO issuance, vendor master data.
- Legal: Contract review, clause library maintenance, signature authority gatekeeping.
- Contract Owner: Acceptance criteria, delivery coordination, operational handoffs.
- Billing Operations: Billing system configuration, invoice issuance, dispute management.

Integrations and automation recommendations
- Use Commitment ID as the single key across systems: Procurement Portal, Contract Repository, Forecast Ledger, Billing System.
- Automate notifications: Signed contract triggers webhook to Finance and Billing to create ledger entries and invoice schedules.
- Audit trail: All approvals and exception notes must be appended to the Commitment record.

Sample JSON snippet to create a Commitment record (example for integrations)
{
  "commitment_id": "CMT-2027-0458",
  "vendor": "Acme GPUs Inc.",
  "amount": "$420,000",
  "term_months": "36",
  "billing_trigger": "provisioning_complete",
  "budget_code": "ENG-RTX-POOL",
  "contract_url": "https://contracts.redwood/cmt-2027-0458"
}

Change control and review cadence
- Annual review: Governance playbook reviewed yearly by Finance, Procurement, Legal, and Security.
- Quarterly KPIs: Procurement and Finance publish a cross-functional KPI dashboard to the Finance Portal.
- Ad-hoc updates: Any material change to revenue recognition rules or procurement thresholds requires Legal + CFO sign-off and update to this playbook.
